To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Phosphate-soubilising bacteria (PSB9, PSB16) inoculated treatments with triple supper phosphate (60 kg P2o5 ha-1) significantly improved plant growth (plant dry matter, root growth and P uptake) and available soil P (P solubilization) as compared with control and PSB inoculated treatments with TSP (30, 60 kg P 2o5 ha -1) and control.
the inoculation of PSB with TSP fertilizer improved the association, P uptake and growth of aerobic rice.
the inoculation of  Bacillus  sp. PSB9 and PS B16 strains in aerobic rice system significantly enhanced plant biomass, P uptake and available soil P.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of phosphate solubilizing bacterial inoculums and triple supper phosphate (TSP) on plant growth, P solubilization and bacterial colonization in aerobic rice.
the effect of different P fertilizers on root colonization and association of PSB in aerobic rice system.
the use of PSB as a potential biofertilizer to enhance P uptake and growth of aerobic and wetland rice.

we have successfully isolated and identified two phosphate solubilizing bacterial strains, namely, PSB9 and PS B16, from Malaysian soil and evaluated the effect of inoculation of these bacteria on the growth of aerobic rice in a greenhouse experiment.
we have been successful to isolate phosphate solubilizing bacterias (PSB) that can solubilize insoluble P from native soil.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we have developed a method for the rapid and accurate identification of bacterial strains based on the 16S rRNA gene, which has been widely used as a standard marker in the classification of bacterial strains.
